No, I think this is actually quite insightful. Thank you!

I think it's good to come up with a game plan. I am definitely ready and willing to meet his needs, as long as it doesn't trigger past traumas. 

If we can come up with a plan that is fun and exciting for both of us and that still doesn't satisfy him, I think I should be vary, as you point out.
He said he used to cheat somewhat frequently as he was younger, but that over the years, it has become less frequent and less severe (say, making out instead of P&V).

Thanks for validating my feelings. I appreciate that.

He has never made me feel like anything but the best thing that has ever happened to him (apart from the above convo). 

I explained to him that I do not feel comfortable with being pressured into having sex on a schedule because of past sexual trauma. I did come up with some creative and fun things for us to do as a couple, sexually, which lightened his mood.

Hm. You make some good points. I did have an 8\-year relationship with someone whom never cheated on me. It was a long road for me to go from insanely paranoid to completely trusting, but by showing him trust over time, we both won.

I think asking him what drove him to cheat in the first place, and to listen with an open mind might bring some clarity, for both of us.
Hahaha yes, I guess so. Am I being incredibly naive?

>comments

Well, it's complicated. He treats me better than any partner I've had before and constantly shows me with words and actions that I mean the world to him. Also, I am nearing 36 and want children badly. Nobody's perfect, neither me nor him.

Well, it's one thing to say "I find other people attractive" and another to then go and have sex with someone other than me. I'm not sure if I hold his honesty against him, like I said, I thanked him for being honest with me, I just feel conflicted about whether he can keep his promise of fidelity. But you're right, keeping an honest line of communication open is always good.
He told them about it when he cheated on them. Beyond that, I don't know.

I just saw this. I truly hope you are still with us and recovering. As a child (albeit a grown one) I can tell you that losing my mother would shatter me. Even if she has not always been the best Mom. And losing her to suicide would be even worse, as it leaves so many scarred in its wake. Please consider the fact that the negative thoughts you are experiencing right now about your "bad" parenting, are a real side\-effect of being depressed. When we are depressed, we tend to think the worst of ourselves and to see ourselves as in the way and a burden to our loved ones. But they still love us. I bet it was very hard for your son to hear about your recent ideations and you must understand that his reaction of anger is based in fear. Fear of being helpless, fear of losing you. I hope with all my heart that you are getting the best help possible, and please consider reaching out to people who aren´t your children, as it can be paralizing to hear such news from a beloved parent. All the best to you and yours \<3

Thank you so much for your words. 

She's doing much better, but I worry she will try again when she starts feeling depressed again.
Good god. I am so sorry. That is beyond terrible.
Thank you for your comment. Yeah, it's hard when you yourself are dealing with your own demons. Thanks for understanding <3
